end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from where it is grown to the plate.
Identified that longer journeys generally use more fuel and create more pollution.
Explained that local food may be fresher because it spends less time travelling.
Suggested choosing local food to reduce food miles; noted that local food can still have limits.
Teach-back was not passed; food comparison and effects needed more practice.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles and linking travel distance with fuel use, pollution, and freshness. They used the method of tracing food from where it is grown to where it is eaten, and correctly explained why local food may be fresher and use less fuel. At first, they connected imported food with being special or tasting better; this was corrected later when they said distance does not add nutrients and chose local food. At home, ask them to compare two foods and name which travelled farther, then give one likely effect.
